subject: Post-demo: latency & scale checks — hosted vs. dedicated recommendation
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fastretail.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + key capacity questions (hosted vs dedicated)

Hi Alicia — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a handful of clarifying questions so we can land a crisp recommendation between Hosted API and Dedicated capacity for FastRetail.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: real-time product search & personalization via a reranker + short completion funnel.
- SLO: interactive feel — target p95 latency in the 80–120 ms window for the full end-to-end inference call.
- Traffic profile: sustained ~180 qps during peak retail hours, short bursts up to ~600 qps for flash sales (burst windows ~30–120s).
- Typical request size: ~100–160 tokens in, ~40 tokens out (average).
- Data sensitivity: includes customer email + PII in a subset of flows.

Clarifying questions (so we can size a pilot exactly):
1) For the 180 qps sustained, is that single-region US (us-east) only? Any multi-region requirement?
2) Can you confirm the expected concurrency distribution (e.g., 95th percentile concurrent requests)? If you don’t have it, a rough per-second distribution helps.
3) Are there any hard SLA constraints from procurement (e.g., contractual p95 target or uptime % we should include in the pilot)?
4) For PII flows: do you require customer-managed keys / VPC-only access, or is assured-in-redwood (dedicated with SOC2 + contract terms) sufficient for the pilot?

Planned next steps from our side:
- Based on your answers, we’ll propose either a Hosted configuration with aggressive autoscaling + caching, or a Dedicated proof-of-concept (reserved GPU pool) with a fallback to Hosted for non-sensitive traffic.
- I’ve attached a short MAP template and our standard SLA pdf to accelerate procurement.
- Suggested technical kickoff: 30 min next week to align telemetry and a small synthetic test plan.

Would you prefer Hosted first (faster time-to-value, then move to Dedicated if needed), or do you want us to size Dedicated right away given PII concerns?

Best,
Dylan
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0162

Attachments: FastRetail-MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood-SLA-template.pdf (pdf)
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fastretail.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fastretail.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + key capacity questions (hosted vs dedicated)

Thanks, Dylan — good summary. Answers below: 

1) Region: US-east primarily. We may want EU later but not for the initial rollout.
2) Concurrency: we currently see ~90 concurrent requests at 95th percent during peak (that maps roughly to the sustained 180 qps if requests are short-lived). Bursts are spiky — historically we've seen up to 600 qps for ~1–2 minutes during promotions.
3) Procurement: no hard SLA written yet; our internal product goal is p95 < 120 ms for user-facing flows. Procurement will want language around uptime but that’s typical.
4) PII: pilot can run under Redwood-managed keys for a technical evaluation, but long term we will require customer-managed KMS and VPC controls for PII-bearing flows.

Can you provide a high-level estimate of whether Hosted can meet the p95 < 120 ms at sustained 180 qps (with the stated token sizes), or whether Dedicated is required? Also want a ballpark of monthly cost for a pilot (2 weeks) on Dedicated vs Hosted.

Alicia
Sr. Engineering Manager — Search & Personalization
FastRetail
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + key capacity questions (hosted vs dedicated)

Looping in a quick internal note to capture our recommendation and pricing posture before Dylan replies to Alicia.

Quick qualification: given p95 target ~120ms and sustained 180 qps + 600 qps bursts, Dedicated looks like the safer path for the pilot. Reasons:
- Predictable latency: Dedicated removes noisy-neighbor variance and lets us size a pool (2xA100 or equivalent) with colocated KV cache and optimized batching kernels to hit p95 at that qps.
- Autoscale: We can configure aggressive burst capacity (burst to X additional GPUs) for short windows.
- Data controls: Since FastRetail will require customer-managed KMS long-term, starting on Dedicated reduces migration friction.

Suggested pilot scope (2-week POC):
- Dedicated reserved pool: 2 GPU nodes with autoscale policy (scale up to 4 during burst windows)
- Test harness: replay of representative traces (we'll provide small runner) + synthetic spike tests to validate p95 and cold-start behavior
- Observability: full telemetry access in Redwood Console; enable token-level latency breakdowns
- Success criteria: p95 <= 120 ms for 95% of synthetic-captured peak windows, and no more than 2x error rate vs baseline
Commercial posture: offer a pilot discount (50% off for the 2-week Dedicated time) and a short-term SLA addendum for evaluation. Ask Sales Ops to surface an internally approved deal_id and pricing grid.

Naomi — please attach the quick pricing sketch and SOC2 link.

Thanks — I’m fine with Dylan sending a short, actionable note to Alicia with that recommendation and the ask to schedule a tech kickoff.

Lauren
Head of Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fastretail.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, procurement@fastretail.com
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + key capacity questions (hosted vs dedicated)

Thanks for the details, Alicia — helpful. Short answer: Dedicated POC recommended.

TL;DR proposal
- Start with a 2-week Dedicated proof-of-concept (POC) sized to sustain ~180 qps with autoscale to handle bursts up to 600 qps.
- We will provision a 2-node GPU pool (optimized inference nodes) with an autoscale policy to add capacity for short burst windows; observability + telemetry included.
- Pricing: pilot discount applied (internal sketch attached). Naomi will follow up with a one-page pricing sketch and SOC2 link.
- For PII-bearing flows: pilot can use Redwood-managed keys for the evaluation; we’ll scope customer-managed KMS + VPC in parallel for long-term cutover.

Next steps
1) I’ll send an invite for a 30 min technical kickoff (propose Tue/Wed next week) to align test traces and telemetry.
2) Naomi will send the pricing sketch + SOC2 artifact and a DocuSign starter if procurement wants.
3) If procurement is OK, Sales Ops will spin up an internal trial deal (FR-2027-311) and provision the Dedicated pool once contract terms are agreed.

Would you like me to include a quick estimated cost range in the kickoff invite, or should Naomi send the sketch first?

Best — looking forward to the kickoff.
Dylan
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
